rationale: EXIST is a low-overhead intra-service tracing observability system using hardware tracing facilities, buffer management, and cluster orchestration. It improves tracing overhead and coverage, not compute kernels.

Mint changes distributed tracing from all-or-nothing sampling to commonality-plus-variability aggregation to reduce trace storage/network volume. The contribution is observability data collection, not kernel-style optimization.

Apophenia automatically identifies traces in task-based runtime dependence analysis to avoid manual annotations and reduce runtime overhead. It optimizes runtime tracing/dependence-analysis behavior rather than compute kernels.

BTrace is a smartphone tracing tool that manages tracing buffers to retain longer continuous traces with low overhead. Its focus is observability tooling and buffer policy, not kernel-style computation.

This paper refreshes Java benchmarks and performance-analysis methodology and evaluates production garbage collectors. It is an empirical benchmark/methodology contribution, not a kernel-level optimization.

Cinnamon accelerates encrypted AI by exploiting parallelism through algorithms, compilers, and scale-out FHE hardware techniques. The compiler/dataflow components are kernel-like for encrypted ML execution, but the contribution is tightly coupled to a proposed scale-out architecture rather than existing software kernels.

PipeLLM is a runtime system that overlaps GPU confidential-computing encryption with LLM serving or fine-tuning using speculative pipelining. It hides encryption/data-transfer overhead around existing LLM systems rather than changing model compute kernels.

FEDORA trains recommendation models with federated learning and ORAM, balancing privacy and performance for embedding-table access. The contribution is privacy-preserving training/data access, not kernel-style optimization.

The paper uses static invariants to distinguish ML prediction errors from attacks in dynamic call-set prediction for debloating/security. It is a security/control-flow framework, not a compute kernel optimization.

CRUSH is a high-level synthesis strategy for sharing functional units in dynamically scheduled dataflow circuits while avoiding deadlock. It optimizes generated hardware circuits, not software kernels or kernel-generating compilers for existing devices.
AMuLeT automatically tests secure speculation countermeasures for leaks in microarchitectural simulators. The work is design-time security testing, not kernel-style performance optimization.

Parendi is an RTL simulator/compiler that partitions and maps cycle-accurate simulation onto many Graphcore IPU cores, optimizing synchronization, communication, and computation. It outputs optimized accelerator execution for simulation kernels on existing IPU hardware.
